from: July book, night 17 (The Letter Before the Lord)
p1: A big army from far-off Assyria came near Jerusalem. Its king sent King Hezekiah a letter.
The letter said, “The Lord you trust will not keep Jerusalem safe.” It was a scary letter. What would Hezekiah do?
Hezekiah carried the letter to the temple, the Lord’s house. There he spread it out before the Lord.
p2: Then Hezekiah prayed, “O Lord, You made heaven and earth. Lean down close and hear me. Please save us, so all the world will know You are the Lord.”
Hezekiah did not hide his worry. He gave it to the Lord. Tonight, bring one worry to Heavenly Father too. He always hears, and He wants to help.
old: A scary enemy king sent King Hezekiah a mean letter. The letter said, “We’re going to win! Your God can’t save you!” Hezekiah felt worried and afraid. What should he do?
Hezekiah didn’t fight or panic. Instead, he took the letter straight to the temple. He spread the letter open before Heavenly Father. “Please, Lord, see this and help us,” he prayed.
Heavenly Father heard Hezekiah’s prayer. He sent the prophet Isaiah with a message: “Don’t be afraid. I will protect this city.” And God did! He saved His people that very night.
When we have a big worry, we can bring it to Heavenly Father. We can “spread it out” before Him in prayer. He listens, and He helps. Taking our troubles to God is always the right thing to do.
